name: Gearbox
text: Add InstantX-ComfyUI’s depth-aware upscaler to EXCAVA’s pipeline first. It preselects the sharpest frames before upscaling, cutting wasted compute on blurry or redundant frames—directly lifting output quality without extra hardware. The trade-off is a small added latency from the depth analysis, but the net gain in clarity per frame justifies it.

name: Torque
text: Depth-aware upscalers won’t fix EXCAVA’s face fidelity drop because the core problem isn’t blur—it’s the model’s inability to preserve identity in low-resolution or heavily compressed frames. The real risk is wasting time on a tool that addresses the wrong symptom while ignoring the actual bottleneck: the base model’s face reconstruction weakness. Test it by running InstantX-ComfyUI on a sample of EXCAVA’s worst face outputs—if face fidelity doesn’t improve, scrap it and push for a face-specific super-resolution model instead.

name: Gearbox

Add Flowframes’ VFI module to EXCAVA’s pipeline first. It directly targets motion smoothness by generating intermediate frames, which raises temporal consistency—a known weak spot in EXCAVA’s output. The trade-off is a small increase in compute per clip, but the module’s lightweight design keeps the hit minimal while delivering measurable gains in perceived fluidity.

name: Torque
text: Flowframes’ VFI won’t fix EXCAVA’s face fidelity drop because it masks motion jitter, not identity loss—it’s a bandage on a core model failure. The real risk is burning cycles on a tool that trades temporal smoothness for sharper but still wrong faces. Settle it by running a blind A/B test: feed the same clip through EXCAVA with and without Flowframes, then have a human judge pick the version with the most accurate faces—no metrics, just the faces that look like the original.
